transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I don’t enjoy my classes or my art anymore, and the things that used to excite me just feel flat and pointless. I just don't know how to get that spark back, or if I even can.
Have you felt this way for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, I feel this way nearly every day, and it has been going on steadily for about eight months now. It really started after I was passed over for a promotion at work, and since then, this heavy, hollow sadness just hasn't lifted.
Have you had any periods of feeling better for at least two months at a time during these past eight months?

No, I haven't had any periods of feeling better. Ever since I was passed over for that promotion eight months ago, these feelings have been pretty steady and continuous. I haven't had any real breaks or relief from it at all.
Besides not enjoying your classes and art, have you also lost interest in other activities or people that you used to care about?

Yes, I've started avoiding department events, canceling art activities with my students, and backing out of community art meet-ups I used to love. I've also become very withdrawn at home, leaving my husband to handle almost all of the household chores because I just don't have the energy or motivation to help.
Have you also noticed a decrease in your ability to feel pleasure from activities, people, or experiences that you used to enjoy, even when you do take part in them?

Yes, absolutely. Even when I force myself to sit down and paint or try to go to an art meet-up, it just feels completely flat and hollow. I usually end up backing out entirely or just staring at a blank canvas because there is no joy in it anymore.
Have you experienced any significant improvement in your mood or energy at any point during these eight months, even for a few days, or has it remained consistently low?

No, it has remained consistently low the entire time without any real breaks or improvements. Even on days when something objectively good happens, like a student thanking me, that heavy, gray feeling just stays there and doesn't lift. I haven't had any moments where my mood or energy actually felt better.
